text:
maria: heads up — seeing inference p99 jump from ~220ms to ~1.4s across several GPU nodes in eastus2 starting 11:37 UTC. grafana trace -> https://grafana.redwood/board/infra?panel=latency (zoomed on gpu-cluster eastus2).

deploy-bot: applied net/qos.yml to 124 hosts in tag=gpu-eastus2 at 11:36:22 UTC (change-id: net-2026-03-18-1136).

kai: ugh, that was the scheduled net upgrade for egress shaping. can anyone ssh into a node and paste `tc qdisc show dev eth0`?

olivia: sshed to gpu-node-07 and ran:
```
$ sudo tc -s qdisc show dev eth0
qdisc tbf 1: root refcnt 2 rate 1000Mbit burst 1600b lat 50ms
 Sent 102345678 bytes  packets 12345 drop 842
 backlog 0b 0p requeues 0
qdisc fq_codel 10: parent 1: limit 10240p flows 1024 quantum 1514 ecn
 Sent 98765432 bytes  packets 9876 drop 0
```
looks like a `tbf` root got inserted with a tiny burst (1600b) which is causing host-level queuing and drops on egress. drop counters on eth0 are high.

tony: that `burst 1600b` is way too small for our inter-node flows (RDMA and large grpc payloads). likely fragments TCP segments and causes retransmits. do we have counters on ib0 (rdma)?

olivia: ib0 is up but small rx err increases: `ibstat` and `ifconfig ib0` show low errors, but kernel dmesg on the host has lots of tcp_retransmit_skb warnings.

maria: correlation: p99 spike aligns exactly with deploy-bot roll. looks like net/qos.yml had an egress policer intended for public facing nodes but was applied to gpu tag by mistake. infra-bot, who ran that rollout?

infra-bot: rollout executed by ansible-playbook `net/rollout.yml` using inventory group `gpu-eastus2` matched hosts by tag; playbook used `roles/net-qos` v2.1.3. change diff includes `qos/egress-policy: enabled` for all hosts.

sre-oncall: immediate mitigation: can we remove root qdisc on the affected hosts? command to run across the fleet: `sudo tc qdisc del dev eth0 root` then `sudo tc qdisc add dev eth0 root fq_codel` — that should drop the bottleneck.

kai: running a canary: removing on gpu-node-07 now.

olivia: can confirm after `tc qdisc del dev eth0 root` and `tc qdisc add dev eth0 root fq_codel` p99 dropped from 1.4s -> 210ms within one minute. traces show fewer retransmits.

maria: rolling back the net/qos.yml change for `gpu-eastus2` now. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/net-config/changes/4321 (rollback commit).

deploy-bot: rollback applied to 124 hosts at 11:52:08 UTC (change-id: net-2026-03-18-1152).

tony: postmortem notes: the rule generator had a filter match that included `tags: gpu` due to a variable mis-evaluation. policy intended for `edge-public` only. other findings: no canary existed for internal host groups, and our ansible tag matching is too permissive.\
maria: action items: (1) add a pre-rollout dry-run that shows `tc qdisc show` diffs for a sample host, (2) add an explicit inventory guard preventing `egress-policy: enabled` on groups matching `gpu*`, (3) increase default tbf burst size if tbf is used for internal paths (suggested: burst >= 64kb), (4) add grafana alert on per-host `tc drop` counter > 10/min. assigning: kai(1,2), tony(3), olivia(4).

olivia: also noticed MTU differences on some hosts after the upgrade: several had `ip link set mtu 1500` applied while cluster expects 9000. not the root cause here but we should include MTU validation in net checks.

kai: will follow up with a safe rollout plan: introduce a canary of 2 hosts, then 10%, 50%, full. and add a post-deploy smoke test for inference SLOs.

maria: thanks team. leaving this thread open for the postmortem doc. :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: incident resolved — latency normalized. will file incident report and link to follow-up.
